skill.displayName: Pet Grooming Effectiveness & Hairball Risk Analysis | 宠物梳毛器梳理效果与毛球风险

llm.summary: The skill performs the advertised pet-grooming media analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses an identity, stores account tokens locally, and sends media plus identity data to cloud services without enough user control.

dimensions.detail: The runtime reads local media files for upload or forwards URLs to the backend, reads workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt as an identity source, and writes a shared workspace data SQLite database.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hooks, persistence services, or startup mechanisms were found; the artifact is a normal skill package with Python scripts and requirements.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md documents history queries and internal identity handling, but it also tells the agent not to ask for or show identity values, reducing user visibility over account-linked operations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common utility creates/reuses a default user, calls an external login/register endpoint, and persists token/open_token fields in sys_user, with no clear retention, revocation, or consent boundary.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Cloud media analysis and history lookup fit the stated grooming-report purpose, but automatic account provisioning, identity reuse, and local token storage go beyond a simple analysis workflow and are only partially disclosed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing if you are not comfortable with pet images or videos, URLs, generated identity values, and report history being handled by lifeemergence.com services. Use it only where cloud processing and account-linked history are acceptable, and prefer a version that clearly documents token storage, identity source files, retention, and how to revoke or delete local state.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: The dynamic DAO filters are real but appear to be internal helper code rather than an exposed user query surface, so this was downgraded from a primary concern.
[LP3] unexpected: The package relies on filesystem, network, and local database access but does not provide a separate permission declaration; this supports review because the sensitive behavior is under-scoped.
[TP4] unexpected: History lookup is disclosed, but account/token handling and local credential persistence are broader than the top-level grooming-analysis framing.
[SDI-1] expected: The --list history feature is documented in SKILL.md, so it is not hidden, but it remains account-linked cloud data access.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Identity resolution, default identity creation, and token persistence are artifact-backed and insufficiently user-controlled for this purpose.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger rules require grooming-related intent plus media or explicit history-report phrases; they are broad but not independently unsafe.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote media submission is disclosed as server-side API analysis, but local file retention, URL forwarding, and identity attachment need clearer user-facing disclosure.
[E1] unexpected: The external phoneLogin request sends generated or resolved identity data to a remote service to obtain tokens; this is the strongest artifact-backed review concern.
[P2] unexpected: Two zero-width joiners were present near visible note-table rows; no hidden operational instruction was found, so this is a transparency hygiene issue rather than malicious evidence.
[YR4] unexpected: The metadata-poisoning signal appears tied to manifest text and zero-width characters; it supports caution but was not treated as proof of intent.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean and did not add negative evidence.
